metadata.title: Sugar #11 — El Niño + Hormuz Compound Thesis
metadata.subtitle: Feb'27 SB calls: 18¢ ×2 (May 22) + 19.5¢ ×1 (Aug 12) — compound thesis

thesis.headline: Aug 30: thesis strengthens on the physical side — Indian monsoon deficit widened to 13% (from 11.5% Aug 1), EU cut 2026/27 sugar production 19% to an 11-year low (13.4 MMT), and Hormuz remains fully disrupted (a Kuwaiti tanker was struck Aug 26) with no ceasefire in sight. Spot holding near the Aug 27 breakout (~18.2¢, 15-month high) through the 18¢ strike; no fresher print confirmed this week.
thesis.summary: No reversal signals found this week — if anything the deficit case widened further even as spot consolidated near its Aug 27 breakout. New this week: the EU Sugar Market Observatory cut its 2026/27 production estimate to 13.4 MMT, down 19% YoY and an 11-year low, adding a fourth independent forecaster (alongside Covrig −300k MT, Green Pool −3.3 MMT, StoneX −1.7 MMT) to the deficit column. The Indian monsoon deficit, which had stalled around 11.5-12% below normal in early August, widened to 13% below normal by Aug 26 (IMD) — East/NE India worst-hit at -27% — with IMD's own outlook pointing to continued below-normal rainfall through September; this is deterioration, not the recovery that would weaken the thesis. NOAA's Aug 13 CPC ENSO diagnostic reconfirmed (did not downgrade) the very-strong-El-Niño call: Niño-3.4 at +1.4°C and still strengthening, >90% odds of a very strong Oct-Dec peak, 69% odds of exceeding every El Niño since 1950. Brazil's UNICA published a 2H-August report (38.31 MMT cane crushed, ethanol output +3.15%) confirming mills are still running hard, but the precise sugar-mix percentage versus last year could not be independently verified this week — treat the ethanol-pivot trend as continuing but the exact number as carried forward from 2H-July (41.4% mix, sugar output -17.6% YoY). India's demand-side response remains the key bearish counterweight: the 1 MMT nil-duty import quota (window Aug 20-Oct 31, corrected from an earlier assumed Sep-Nov window) plus the Aug 26 diversion of 3.5 lakh tonnes of export sugar to the domestic market are real supply relief, with the Oct 31 quota-enlargement decision the next catalyst to watch. Hormuz stays fully disrupted — a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker (Al Salam II) was struck Aug 26 transiting the Strait, and Trump's Aug 25 claim that all mines were cleared is disputed by JMIC — so the ceasefire-driven IV-crash exit trigger has not fired; nearby-tenor options IV (Jul '26 ~31%, Oct '26 ~23%) sits inside the normal 18-35% band, though Feb/Mar'27-specific IV (the position's actual tenor) could not be sourced this week. Spot is at/just through the 18¢ strike but still below both call breakevens (18.88¢ and 20.30¢); the 200%-profit-take trigger cannot be confirmed without current option marks.

elNino.probabilityWindow: El Niño Advisory ACTIVE (NOAA CPC, Aug 2026) — event formed and intensifying
elNino.strongEventOdds: 95% very strong (Niño 3.4/RONI ≥ +2.0°C) — up from 81% in July's CPC assessment; 69% chance RONI reaches +2.5°C+, which would exceed every El Niño on record since 1950
elNino.soiNote: NOAA's Aug RONI forecast puts the median Oct-Dec value at +2.66°C (middle 50% range +2.37 to +2.95°C); little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027

millMix.brazilOutputNote: 2026/27 through May: sugar mix collapsed to 41.4% (from 50.1% a year ago) as mills pivot to ethanol — C-S sugar output 6.84 MMT, -2.0% YoY. This is the 'mill mix shift' leg of the tail scenario actually happening. 2H-July update: crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. USDA's full-season 2026/27 Sugar Annual still projects the mix averaging closer to 48% sugar / 52% ethanol for the year — meaning the mid-year prints (41.4%, -17.6%) are running well below even that already-bearish full-season forecast. 2H-August UNICA report: 38.31 MMT cane crushed (down 14.56% vs 1H-August, a normal seasonal sequential decline), ethanol production up 3.15% to 1.77 billion liters — mills are still running at scale. The precise sugar-mix percentage versus last year for this fortnight could not be independently verified this week (some secondary sources point directionally lower, toward the low-30s%, but that figure is unconfirmed) — treat the pivot as continuing, with the hard 41.4%/-17.6% 2H-July figures as the last confirmed data point.

historicalContext.event: Aug 27 breakout to 18.21¢ — 15-mo high through the 18¢ strike; record OI, El Niño odds 90%/65% 'historic'

catalystTimeline.event: Indian monsoon — LIVE, DETERIORATING: cumulative deficit widened to 13% below normal (Aug 26, IMD) from ~11.5% (Aug 1) — the earlier stall has reversed into further shortfall; East/NE India worst-hit at -27%. IMD's outlook still points below 94% of the long-period average through Aug-Sep
India CONFIRMED: 1 MMT nil-duty raw import quota (first in ~10 yrs) + bulk stockholding limits Sep 1–Nov 30. Next catalyst: quota extension/enlargement if 1 MMT proves insufficient
El Niño peak intensity — NOAA: very strong peak likely Oct–Jan (63% ≥ +2.0°C)

managementRules: Profit-take 1: Sell 50% at 200% return on premium
Stop trigger: IV crashes below 18% on ceasefire news
Time stop: Reassess at 60 DTE if not ITM

exitTriggers.name: El Niño weakens / fails
exitTriggers.rationale: Was the primary risk — now essentially retired: NOAA's Aug update raised the odds of a very-strong Oct-Dec peak to 95% (from 81% in July), with a 69% chance of exceeding every El Niño on record since 1950. Persistence holds at 97% through early spring 2027. Residual risk is now just a peak that undershoots this already-elevated forecast, not a failure of the event itself.

exitTriggers.name: Hormuz ceasefire IV crush
exitTriggers.rationale: Options re-price down even before underlying moves. Pre-expiry risk. No de-escalation this week — a Kuwaiti-flagged tanker (Al Salam II) was struck transiting the Strait on Aug 26, and Trump's Aug 25 claim that all mines were cleared is disputed by JMIC; the Strait remains effectively closed to normal commercial traffic. Nearby-tenor options IV (Jul/Oct '26, ~23-31%) remains inside the normal band, no crush observed.

exitTriggers.name: Brazilian mill mix stays at sugar
exitTriggers.rationale: Largely retired — mills have pivoted hard to ethanol: 2H-July crush -8.4% YoY, sugar output -17.6% YoY, with the ethanol blend mandate raised to 32%. Residual risk is a mix reversal if ethanol parity flips.

exitTriggers.name: India ethanol policy reversal
exitTriggers.rationale: Govt raises diversion → removes export supply (bullish risk for sugar but kills bear setup).

exitTriggers.name: Theta decay without move
exitTriggers.rationale: ~$3-5/day per OTM call. Manageable but compounds if no move by Q4.

tailScenario.title: Energy Lockdown → Sugar Deficit

components.mechanism: Brazilian mill mix shift to ethanol

tailScenario.context: 2024/25 deficit was 3.5 MMT → drove sugar +100% to 28¢. Lockdown deficit could be 2-3x larger.
tailScenario.inelasticDemandNote: Sugar is staple food. COVID: consumption fell 3-5%, recovered fast. 1973-74 energy crisis: consumption fell <10%, prices rose 6x.
